target.title: [codex] Use Executing for default progress label
target.body:
## Summary

- Replace the themed default progress draft label pool with neutral technical labels (`Working`, `Reading`, `Checking`, `Running`, `Testing`, `Reviewing`, `Updating`, `Inspecting`, `Searching`, `Planning`, `Analyzing`, `Verifying`, `Preparing`, `Loading`, `Scanning`, `Executing`, `Syncing`, `Building`, `Finishing`, `Reporting`).
- Keep the existing config surface and document the exact commentary-without-tools mode: `streaming.mode: "progress"`, `streaming.progress.commentary: true`, and `streaming.progress.toolProgress: false`.
- Document hidden/easy user customization through the existing `$include` mechanism, for example `~/.openclaw/progress-draft-preferences.json5` included from each channel's `streaming.progress`.
- Store commentary progress as plain text instead of Markdown `_..._` wrappers, and cover Telegram rich-preview fallback text so raw underscores do not leak into visible drafts.

Fixes #94850.

## Why

Issue #94850 is broader than one default label. Users need progress drafts that can show Codex-level commentary without exposing tool calls, while defaults should be product-neutral and custom terms should remain easy to set outside the already-large main config. The Telegram screenshot also showed raw `_..._` leaking into the plain preview path; this makes commentary plain at the shared compositor/formatter boundary and lets rich renderers style it from structured line metadata.

## Real Behavior Proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Progress drafts use neutral default labels; commentary remains opt-in; `toolProgress: false` hides tool/task lines while allowing configured commentary; Telegram rich fallback text does not expose raw `_Checking..._`.
- **Real environment tested:** Lexar worktree `/Volumes/LEXAR/repos/worktrees/openclaw-pr-94859-progress-drafts`, rebased on current `origin/main`, PR head `e7412a41e4`.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.channels.config.ts src/channels/progress-draft-compositor.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.plugin-sdk.config.ts src/plugin-sdk/channel-streaming.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-telegram.config.ts telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
  - `node --import tsx scripts/generate-bundled-channel-config-metadata.ts --check`
  - `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 <touched TypeScript/generated files>`
- **Evidence after fix:**
  - Compositor focused suite: `15 passed`.
  - Plugin SDK formatter suite: `29 passed`.
  - Telegram dispatch suite: `168 passed`.
  - Generated channel config metadata check: `exit_status=0`.
  - Format check: `exit_status=0`.
  - GitHub checks on `e7412a41e4`: `Real behavior proof`, `auto-response`, `dispatch`, `dependency-guard`, `dependency-guard-detect`, `label`, `security-sensitive-guard`, and `security-sensitive-guard-detect` passed; non-applicable Mantis/label helper jobs skipped.
- **Observed result after fix:** The shared runtime default pool is neutral, custom `progress.label` / `progress.labels` remain supported, commentary-only progress drafts render without tool lines, and Telegram rich fallback text is `Shelling\n\n💬 Checking recent context` rather than `Shelling\n\n_Checking recent context_`.
- **What was not tested:** No live customer/runtime release; this PR proves shared formatter/config behavior and Telegram dispatch preview rendering.

## Validation Notes

- The first local command from the plan used `--runInBand`, but this repo's current Vitest CLI rejects that option. Focused local runs used `--maxWorkers=1`.
- `pnpm config:channels:check` attempted to install because this short-lived worktree uses an ignored `node_modules` symlink; the underlying generated metadata check was run directly and passed.
